question.prompt: Alice, Bob, and Charlie were on a hike and were wondering how far away the nearest town was. When Alice said, “We are at least \(6\) miles away,” Bob replied, “We are at most \(5\) miles away.” Charlie then remarked, “Actually the nearest town is at most \(4\) miles away.” It turned out that none of the three statements was true. Let \(d\) be the distance in miles to the nearest town. Which of the following intervals is the set of all possible values of \(d?\)

solutions.title: Combine the false statements
solutions.explanation:
Because every statement is false, each claimed inequality must be negated, including its equality case:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Alice: }&d\ge6\text{ is false, so }d<6,\\
\text{Bob: }&d\le5\text{ is false, so }d>5,\\
\text{Charlie: }&d\le4\text{ is false, so }d>4.
\end{aligned}
\]
The condition \(d>5\) already guarantees \(d>4\). Thus all three conditions hold exactly when
\[
5<d<6.
\]
The interval is \(\boxed{(5,6)}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
